_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The facility is currently owned and operated by Midstream LPG Inc. (Midstream). The site functions as a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) terminal, where propane is delivered by rail car and transferred to transports utilizing self-contained mobile transloader units. It is intended that up to four (4) rail cars be on site at any time. Facility operations are subject to OSHA PSM and EPA RMP Program Level 3 requirements, due to the quantity of propane, a regulated flammable substance, present in the transload process exceeding 10,000 lbs and the potential for a worst-case scenario to impact a public receptor.

THE FACILITY AND THE REGULATED SUBSTANCE HANDLED
The Buckeye LPG Terminal receives LPG (propane) delivered by rail cars, up to four (4) on site at any time. The propane is transloaded directly from each rail car to a transport tanker utilizing a mobile transloader unit engineered for the purpose. Propane is loaded onto transports for distribution. To minimize emissions during unloading operations, a vapor balance system between the rail car and transport is employed to minimize the release of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). The facility normally operates 8 hours/day, 5 days a week unless occasional market demands require extending operating hours.

The worst-case flammable scenario for the facility is based on the release of 130,000 lbs of propane from a single rail car. Propane, a regulated flammable substance under both the RMP and PSM, is present on site in quantities that classify the facility as a Program Level 3 process.

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM
The accidental release prevention program is based on the requirements of Title 40 CFR, Part 68. The program includes the following elements, Offsite Consequence Analysis, Employee Participation, Process Safety Information, Process Hazard Analysis, Operating Procedures, Training, Contractor Evaluation, Contractors and Visitor Orientation, Pre Startup Safety Review, Mechanical Integrity, Code of Safe Wo

rk Practices (Hot Work Permit, Confined Space Entry, and Control of Hazardous Energy), Management of Change, Incident Investigation, Emergency Planning and Response, and Compliance Audits.

Midstream maintains an emergency response plan in compliance with local emergency response agencies. Training includes employee responsibilities in the PSM and RMP programs, emergency response, hot work permit procedures, code of safe work practices, and operating procedures.
The process maintains mitigation measures consisting of relief valves, check valves, manual shut offs, automatic shutoffs, startup and operating procedures, and grounding equipment.

EXTERNAL EVENTS ANALYSIS

Earthquake hazards have been considered in the external events analysis. It is understood that the general seismicity of the area is low, but there is the possibility of significant earthquakes from time to time. Operations are conducted outdoors with minimal exposure to collapsing structures or falling objects. In the event a significant earthquake is experienced, operators are trained to cease any product transfers, secure equipment, and relocate to a safe area.

Flood hazards have been considered in the external events analysis. According to information available through the Maricopa County Floodplain and Elevation Certificate Viewer, the facility site is outside the 100-year flood zone and is designated Effective Floodplain: X. This corresponds to being outside the 0.2% annual chance floodplain. While flooding at the site is expected to be low risk, operators are trained to cease any product transfers, secure equipment, and relocate to a safe area in the event of severe weather.

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICY
An accidental release prevention and emergency response policy has been established by Midstream management and implemented by the employees. In the event of an accidental release, the terminal operators are trained to shut off the source from a safe location or ac

tivate one of the emergency shutdown devices, contact 911, and secure the area. The 911 system is used to notify the fire department.

EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM
Midstream maintains an emergency response plan in compliance with local emergency response agencies.

FIRE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
This a newly operational LPG Terminal and has not had any accidental releases.

PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
Planned changes to improve safety have been established based on process safety management audits, employee safety observations, and the process hazard analysis.

WORST CASE SCENARIO
A worst-case flammable release scenario was modeled for propane, a regulated flammable gas stored as a pressurized liquid at quantities above the 10,000-lb threshold. The scenario involved the catastrophic failure of a single rail car containing 130,000 lbs of propane. Using the EPA's browser-based RMP*Comp tool, the 1 psi overpressure endpoint distance was calculated to be 0.4 miles. Using satellite imagery and Maricopa County Assessor Parcel data, it was estimated that approximately 20 residents could be within the worst-case scenario endpoint distance. This area of Maricopa County is sparsely populated and detailed population data could not be found. Due to the presence of public receptors, the flammable nature of the substance, and the facility's coverage under PSM/RMP, this process is classified as a Program Level under EPA's Risk Management Program.

ALTERNATE RELEASE SCENARIO
An alternative flammable release scenario was modeled for propane, based on a rupture or disconnection of a transfer hose during transloading operations. The scenario involves the release of approximately 115 lbs of propane, which could lead to a vapor cloud explosion (VCE). Using the EPA's browser based RMP*Comp tool, the 1 psi overpressure endpoint distance was estimated at 0.02 miles. Due to the siting of the transload operations on site, this endpoint does not extend beyond the terminal boundary fence, and

no public receptors are impacted. This scenario represents a more realistic, though less severe, event compared to the worst-case scenario and helps inform emergency planning and mitigation strategies. The transloader PHAs consider the causes, consequences, and safeguards for this alternate release scenario.

MANAGEMENT COMMITMENT
Midstream has a commitment to employee and public safety. This commitment is demonstrated by maintaining the implementation of the process and safety requirements already in place. Furthermore, the resources invested in accident prevention, such as training personnel and considering safety in design during construction and installations, is an investment in good business practices. Midstream's policy is to implement reasonable controls to prevent foreseeable releases. However, if a release does occur, trained personnel will respond to control and contain the release.
